title: AI Consulting in Practice – NLW, Superintelligent, @AIDailyBrief⁩

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk centers on enterprise AI adoption patterns, ROI measurement, and how organizations derive value from AI use cases rather than on technical model or systems engineering.

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk centers on enterprise AI adoption patterns, ROI measurement, and how organizations derive value from AI use cases rather than on technical model or systems engineering.

summary: NLW opens by framing the discussion against AI bubble narratives, drawing on his dual perspective as a macro-level AI news analyst and ground-level consultant interviewing executives. He reviews enterprise AI adoption status, citing KPMG data showing production agent deployment rising from 11% in Q1 to 42% in Q3 among billion-dollar-plus companies, and McKinsey data showing only 7% of organizations at full scale while 62% remain in experimentation or piloting. He notes a significant 2025 inflection in coding and software engineering adoption spreading beyond engineering teams, and observes that larger organizations are scaling faster than smaller ones. A key theme is the bifurcation between leaders who adopt comprehensively and laggards doing spot experiments. AI spend is increasing, with KPMG respondents planning $130 million average spend over 12 months, and Deloitte showing 90%+ plan to increase spending. CEO ROI expectations have pulled forward dramatically, with 67% now expecting ROI in 1-3 years versus 63% expecting 3-5 years previously. However, 78% report traditional impact metrics struggle with AI's new reality. To address this gap, NLW launched a self-reported study collecting roughly 2,500 use cases from over 1,000 organizations. Early findings show 44.3% seeing modest ROI, 37.6% seeing high ROI, and only 5% reporting negative ROI. Time savings represents about 35% of use cases, clustering around 5 hours saved. Deeper analysis reveals that organizations of 200-1,000 people concentrate more on increasing output, while C-suite and senior leaders focus less on time savings and more on new capabilities, with 17% of their use cases reporting transformational impact. Smallest organizations (1-50 people) show more transformational benefit early. Coding and software use cases outperform average ROI with lower negative ROI. Risk reduction, though only 3.4% of use cases, has the highest transformational outcome rate at 25%. Healthcare and manufacturing show meaningfully higher impact than average. Agentic and automation use cases wildly outperform in self-reported ROI. Organizations submitting more use cases tend to see better ROI, reinforcing the value of systematic cross-organizational adoption over spot experiments. The full study is expected in early December.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Context
sections.summary: NLW introduces the topic of practical AI value in organizations, contrasting it with AI bubble narratives. He brings dual perspectives: macro-level analysis from the AI Daily Brief podcast and ground-level insights from executive interviews at Superintelligent.

sections.title: Enterprise AI Adoption Status
sections.summary: Reviews enterprise adoption trends, highlighting the 2025 coding/software engineering inflection and agent deployment growth from 11% to 42% (KPMG). Notes shifts in human-agent interaction, upskilling emphasis, and decreased resistance, while most organizations remain stuck in pilot phases.

sections.title: Scaling Challenges and Leader-Laggard Bifurcation
sections.summary: Cites McKinsey data showing only 7% at full scale, 62% experimenting or piloting. Larger organizations are scaling faster than smaller ones. Leaders distinguish themselves through comprehensive, systematic adoption and revenue/capability thinking beyond simple time savings.

sections.title: AI Spend and ROI Expectations
sections.summary: AI spend is increasing: KPMG shows planned spend rising to $130M, Deloitte shows 90%+ increasing spend. CEO ROI expectations have pulled forward dramatically. However, 78% report traditional metrics struggle with AI's new reality, motivating NLW's ROI study.

sections.title: ROI Study Design and Early Findings
sections.summary: Launched late October, collected ~2,500 use cases from 1,000+ organizations across eight impact categories. Findings: 44.3% modest ROI, 37.6% high ROI, ~5% negative ROI. 67% expect high ROI growth. Time savings dominates at 35% of use cases, clustering around 5 hours saved.

sections.title: ROI by Organization Size and Role
sections.summary: Organizations of 200-1,000 people concentrate more on increasing output use cases. C-suite and senior leaders focus less on time savings and more on new capabilities, with 17% of their use cases reporting transformational impact. Smallest organizations (1-50 people) show more transformational benefit early; NLW plans a follow-up study to dig deeper into this segment.

sections.title: Use Case Category Deep Dives and Industry Patterns
sections.summary: Coding and software use cases outperform average ROI with lower negative ROI. Risk reduction, though only 3.4% of use cases, has the highest transformational outcome at 25%. Healthcare and manufacturing show meaningfully higher impact than the cross-organization average. Study available at roisurvey.ai.

sections.title: Agentic ROI, Systematic Adoption, and Wrap-Up
sections.summary: Agentic and automation use cases wildly outperform in self-reported ROI, signaling a trend toward more advanced applications. Organizations submitting more use cases tend to see better ROI, reinforcing the value of systematic cross-organizational adoption over spot experiments. Full study expected early December. NLW expresses excitement about moving from generic impact conversations toward more rigorous experiments.
